s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal pain with liver dysfunction and a large cystic liver tumor
salient_findings: Elevated alkaline phosphatase and γ-glutamyl transferase
Large cystic liver tumor with solid components
key_facts: Negative hepatitis B and C viral markers
Normal α-fetoprotein, PIVKA-II, CEA, and CA19-9 levels
Abdominal CT showed a 16 cm cystic tumor in the liver
MRI showed mixed high and low signal intensity
Abdominal ultrasound demonstrated a honeycomb-like tumor
PET–CT showed FDG uptake in the solid components of the cyst

shortlist.label: Mucinous cystadenocarcinoma of the liver
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging findings of a large cystic tumor with septa and solid components, elevated DUPAN-2 and CA125 levels

shortlist.label: Hepatic sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging findings of a large cystic tumor with solid components, PET-CT showed FDG uptake in the solid components

shortlist.label: Biliary cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging findings of a large cystic tumor with septa and solid components, elevated CA125 levels

shortlist.label: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated alkaline phosphatase and γ-glutamyl transferase levels, imaging findings of a large cystic tumor

shortlist.label: Hepatobiliary cystadenoma with malignant transformation
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging findings of a large cystic tumor with septa and solid components, elevated DUPAN-2 and CA125 levels

raw.rationale: The patient's imaging findings, including a large cystic tumor with solid components and septa, and the presence of elevated DUPAN-2 and CA125 levels, are consistent with mucinous cystadenocarcinoma of the liver. The tumor's appearance on CT, MRI, and ultrasound, as well as the FDG uptake on PET-CT, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hepatic sarcoma
rejected.why: While sarcoma is a possibility, the presence of mucinous components and the specific tumor markers suggest mucinous cystadenocarcinoma is more likely

rejected.label: Biliary cystadenocarcinoma
rejected.why: This diagnosis is possible but less likely given the specific location and characteristics of the tumor, which are more consistent with a primary liver tumor

rejected.label: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
rejected.why: The tumor's appearance and the patient's laboratory results do not strongly suggest intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, which typically presents with more pronounced bile duct obstruction and different tumor markers

rejected.label: Hepatobiliary cystadenoma with malignant transformation
rejected.why: While this is a possible diagnosis, the presence of malignant features and the specific tumor markers make mucinous cystadenocarcinoma a more direct and likely diagnosis
